mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 shows sustained growth over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production by more than 2% within two months signals a supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as production disruptions impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer and construction sectors drive economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both HOUST and RSAFS show increases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a stagflationary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as high inflation erodes purchasing power and high interest rates slow economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when CPIAUCSL is above 5% annualized and FEDFUNDS is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as wage pressures and consumer spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases within a month.
